motion.name: ease-out

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)

motion.name: header-adapt
motion.value: background-color and color 0.4s ease; transparent over the home hero until 24px of scroll; hides (translateY -101%, 0.6s ease-out) past 480px when scrolling down

motion.name: weft-wipe
motion.value: transform scaleX(0 to 1) from left, 0.5s ease-out
motion.purpose: Button hover. Horizontal = weft = Germany.

motion.name: warp-wipe
motion.value: transform scaleY(0 to 1) from bottom, 0.5s ease-out
motion.purpose: Chapter tab hover. Vertical = warp = Africa.

motion.name: data-split
motion.value: lines yPercent 130 to 0, 1.1s expo.out, stagger 0.09s, once at top 90%; each mask padded 0.08em above and 0.17em below
motion.purpose: Headline lines rise out of their mask. The padding keeps descenders and umlaut dots uncut.

motion.name: data-rv
motion.value: y 36px + fade, 1.1s expo.out, stagger 0.07s (kids), once at top 88%
motion.purpose: Blocks and list children rise in.

motion.name: data-rv-weft
motion.value: xPercent -14 + fade, 1.1s expo.out, stagger 0.11s
motion.purpose: Statement lines slide in from the left.

motion.name: data-grow
motion.value: scaleX 0 to 1 from left, 1.3s expo.out
motion.purpose: A ribbon bar draws in.

motion.name: data-count
motion.value: text set to 0 at once, then 0 to n, 1.8s expo.out, once at top 80%
motion.purpose: The team figure waits at zero and counts up once when it is seen.

motion.name: data-parallax / data-shift
motion.value: yPercent or xPercent from +n to -n, scrubbed across the section
motion.purpose: Models drift vertically; the closing word drifts sideways.

motion.name: sheet-stack
motion.value: position: sticky; top: min(0, 100vh - sheet height)
motion.purpose: Sheets stack on screens of 1089px and wider with motion allowed. Covered sheets are never dimmed.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.value: Lenis lerp 0.11; anchor glide 1.4s; a new page starts at scroll 0, back and forward keep the browser's place, hash links keep their target
motion.purpose: Only when motion is allowed.

motion.name: hero-film
motion.value: video fades in over the still, opacity 0.45s; seconds 0 to 5 play once, then the film repeats from second 5
motion.purpose: The ribbons weave in once. After that only the living scene repeats. Pausable.

motion.name: hero-leave
motion.value: media scale 1 to 1.12, copy yPercent -28 and fade, scrubbed over one screen
motion.purpose: The hero as the next sheet covers it. Wide screens only.

motion.name: country-track
motion.value: pinned 280svh, track x scrubbed 0.5; models rotate ±5deg to ∓3deg
motion.purpose: Seven countries pulled sideways by the scroll.

motion.name: weave-scene
motion.value: pinned 250svh, progress glided 0.6s power2.out; start state rendered at once, every band outside the screen; horizontal bands from the left and right screen edges (1s, stagger 0.1), vertical bands from below and every third from above (1s, stagger 0.06), coast shapes scale in (0.6s back.out(1.6))
motion.purpose: The logo weaves itself beside its sentence. On small screens the bands come only from the sides and from below, and it plays once at 0.8 speed.

motion.name: ship-scene
motion.value: ship x from -108vw to 0, 2.6s power3.out, once when the chapter is half a screen away; headline lines yPercent 130 to 0 at 1.15s (1.2s expo.out, stagger 0.1); side text y 28 + fade at 1.45s; then y -10 and 0.35deg, 3.4s sine.inOut yoyo; xPercent -3 to 4 scrubbed
motion.purpose: The container ship sails in from the left screen edge, then the words come up. Home Cloody chapter and Cloody page opening.

motion.name: logo-trail
motion.value: tile scale 0.5 to 1 (0.35s back.out(1.8)), glides on 1.5s power3.out, scale to 0 (0.45s power2.in); one self-drawn loop of 3.2s before the first mouse move
motion.purpose: Mouse and motion allowed only: the cursor leaves the client logos behind as a trail. Elsewhere the marquee runs.

motion.name: energy-film
motion.value: 61 stills on a canvas, scrubbed 0.5 by the scroll; pinned (wrapper 230svh, sticky 100svh stage) at 1089px wide and 44rem tall with motion allowed, else scrubbed from top 68% to top 8%; track bar scaleX = progress; caption swaps at 0.5 (out 0.2s, in 0.35s after 0.2s); chips fill at 0.36 / 0.56 / 0.8
motion.purpose: The company building from today to after the consultation. Runs forwards and backwards. No clip-path on the pictures.

motion.name: marquee
motion.value: translateX(-100%), 70s linear infinite, pausable
motion.purpose: The row of 32 client logos.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all durations 0.01ms; no Lenis, no stack, no hero film, no sailing ship, no logo trail; the energy film is two stills; nothing hidden
motion.purpose: The still state of every moving part.

narrative.northStar: Weißes Modell, fünf Bänder (white model, five ribbons)
narrative.overview:
The SIFK world is a matte-white scale model, like the card-and-plaster models architects build. The only colour in it is the five ribbons of the woven logo: ink, red-orange, gold, lime and green. A ribbon never decorates. It is a whole flat field that owns a chapter of the page.

Pages are built like sheets of coloured paper on a model-maker's table. Each section is one full-width field. On wide screens the next sheet slides over the one before it. Pictures are photographs of white models with paper ribbons in exactly those five colours. They are cut out and stand directly on a field.
keyCharacteristics: Flat full-bleed colour fields, one per chapter.
White model photographs standing on those fields, with only their own cast shadow.
Very large condensed headlines in Barlow Condensed 700.
Square corners everywhere (radius 0). The only round shape is a country flag.
Motion taken from the logo: sideways is the weft (Germany), up-and-down is the warp (Africa).
One next step on every page: request a first call.

rules.name: The Whole Field Rule
rules.body: A ribbon colour is a whole flat surface: a section, a tile, a band or a solid ribbon bar. It is never a tint, a gradient, a glow or a coloured icon box.

rules.name: The Black On Red Rule
rules.body: Text on Glut is always `#000`. Ink on Glut is about 4.4:1 and fails AA for normal text. Black is about 4.8:1 and passes. Running text on Glut is weight 500, not 400, so the black letters keep their outline on red. Headlines and labels keep their own weight.

rules.name: The Inverse Button Rule
rules.body: A button takes its field's text colour as background and its field's colour as label. Never give a button its own colour. One exception: on Glut the label is white, because red on black is too dim to read.

rules.name: The Guest Colours Rule
rules.body: Two guests keep their own colours. The 32 client logos stand only on the white field, as one moving row or as the cursor trail. The seven round country flags stand only next to a country name or on a person tile. Both are signs to be recognised, not decoration. Nothing else brings its own colours.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase styling and no wide letter-spacing anywhere. Headlines are sentences with a full stop.

rules.name: The Balance Rule
rules.body: Headlines use `text-wrap: balance`. Reading text uses `text-wrap: pretty` and a line-length cap in `ch`.

rules.name: The One Field Per Chapter Rule
rules.body: A section is one colour from edge to edge. Change the colour only when the chapter changes.

rules.name: The Never Dimmed Rule
rules.body: A sheet that is being covered keeps its full colour. No overlay, no fade, no blur on covered sheets.

rules.name: The Model Shadow Only Rule
rules.body: Only a model photograph casts a shadow. Buttons, cards, tiles, the header and the menu never do.

rules.name: The Still First Rule
rules.body: Every moving part has a complete still state. With reduced motion there is no smooth scroll, no film, no stacking, no sailing ship, no logo trail, the energy film is two stills, and the logo stands finished.

rules.name: The Hide Only When Moving Rule
rules.body: Content is hidden before its reveal only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, and only until the motion layer is ready. A timer shows everything after 3.5s if the script never starts.

rules.name: The Pause Rule
rules.body: Whatever keeps moving by itself gets a visible pause button.

dos: Do give each chapter one whole flat field from the seven field classes.
Do set text on Glut in `#000` and weight 500, on Ink and Laub in white, on Gold, Lime, Plaster and White in ink.
Do keep every corner square (radius 0). The round country flags are the one exception.
Do give every section a field class, so the header can take its colour.
Do stand model photographs directly on a field with only their cast `drop-shadow`.
Do move sideways for weft and Germany, and up-and-down for warp and Africa.
Do give every motion a still fallback and every loop a pause button.
Do keep headlines large: Mega for chapters, Display for sections, in Barlow Condensed 700.
Do keep the desktop first viewport and the full-bleed ribbon fields with model photographs as they are.
Do log the prompt of every new picture in `asset-library/08-maquette/PROMPTS.md` and in a `.webp.json` next to the file.
donts: Don't use a ribbon colour as a tint, a gradient, a glow or a coloured icon box.
Don't add `box-shadow` to any interface part. Only models cast shadows.
Don't round corners, soften colours or shrink type. Only a country flag is round.
Don't use a flag as decoration or put one in a model picture. A flag stands next to a country name or on a person tile.
Don't dim, fade or blur a sheet while the next one covers it.
Don't hide content before a reveal when reduced motion is on.
Don't use Amber outside the logo drawing.
Don't use stock photographs, golden-hour photos, pattern strips or dark consulting layouts.
Don't invent team portraits, clients, quotes or figures. People are shown as initials on their country's colour.

Don't touch the SEO layer: `lib/seo.ts`, `app/sitemap.ts`, `app/robots.ts`, `lib/structured-data.ts`, `lib/locale-routing.ts`, any `app//page.tsx`, the 16 routes, or the anchors `#internationale-geschaeftsentwicklung` and `#energieberatung-deutschland`.
